results.evidence: Fifth pass, 2026-09-30, using an ordinary browser view. The 2006 NWHikers thread ('Bald Eagle Peak (Point 6,259) 7.14.06') now loads and was read in full. It describes the North Ridge: 2nd-growth forest, ~700 vertical ft of brush, then the open ridge, then 'Dropping off the ridge to the E' onto snow patches, then a final 800 ft. It gives 5.4 mi RT and 4,689 ft gain, but publishes NO coordinate, track or map. The SummitPost peak page, read in the browser, gives only the summit (47.61687,-121.27163) and driving directions. It calls GPS essential gear but links no GPX. Its North Ridge route child page could not be read: the browser extension has no read permission on that domain, and plain fetch returns 403. Peakbagger stays on a Cloudflare verification page that does not clear in a real browser (not bypassed). A search across CalTopo, Gaia GPS, Strava, AllTrails and Wikiloc returned only the unrelated Alberta Bald Eagle Peak. The 2019 hiking-blog report gives heights only, and its 'GPS track: available' leads to a photo album. So there is still no published coordinate for the 5,400 ft cliff band / bypass gully or the 6,100 ft ridge regain, let alone two. Note for the owner (not a source): pins 2-4 have fractional coordinates with a denominator of 11 (e.g. 47.61587372727273). That is the mark of points interpolated between stored pins, not measured positions. The 2006 account ('dropping off the ridge to the E') agrees the bypass is on the east side, so the pins are not demonstrably off the line. No ops.

Fifth pass, 2026-09-30. Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide (Stevens Pass to Rainy Pass) was reached through Google Books search-inside snippets. Its Rimrock Ridge entry (2000 ed. p.259; 1987 ed. p.239) reads: 'Rimrock Ridge is a high area, generally above 6500 ft, with a zigzagging ground outline. The ridge divides Flat and West Fork Agnes Creeks, and logically extends from Old Guard for some 5 mi. NE. The highest point is 3.2 mi. NE of Sentinel Peak; there is a NE point (7080 ft+), and a summit to the SW (7100 ft+). Climbing history is incomplete, but it is known Dwight Watson, in summer 1936 ...'. The snippet stops there, and Google then served a CAPTCHA, which was not solved. The book's high-routes section (2000 p.386; 1987 p.365) says Rimrock Ridge 'has been used as a hiking exit to the area; it is a moderately difficult alpine and cross-country route', from the Le Conte-Sentinel saddle. An independent source, The Mountaineer annual (1981, p.92), reports a party on 'Rimrock Ridge and Seven Sisters Ridge', which 'form the divide between Flat Creek and the West Fork of Agnes Creek'; it says 'Rimrock Ridge was climbed on August 25'. A third source, the Sierra Club Wilderness Handbook (1967) and Sierra Club Bulletin (1968), describes an outing that crosses Rimrock Ridge and descends the West Fork of Agnes Creek. So two independent sources (Beckey; The Mountaineer 1981) place the ridge between Flat Creek and the WEST FORK of Agnes Creek, NW of the main Agnes Creek valley. The stored approach goes up the main Agnes Creek trail to Swamp Creek Camp (mile ~8.5), then 'bushwhack east into the upper Agnes Creek/Blue Basin drainage', fording Agnes or Spruce Creek. That is the wrong valley, on the far (south-east) side of Agnes Mountain. It is the Agnes Mountain approach, as the row's own data_quality.gaps[0] admits. But no source read gives an actual approach line to Rimrock (which fork trail, where to leave it, how to gain the ridge). They give only the drainages it divides and say it is a cross-country high route, so no replacement approach text can be written from two sources. No ops. Owner options are unchanged. One: replace the approach/itinerary leg with a statement that no route to the ridge is published beyond its lying between Flat Creek and the West Fork of Agnes Creek. Two: if that leg goes, drop the Swamp Creek Camp waypoint (index 2) and Fivemile Camp (index 1).

results.evidence: Fifth pass, 2026-09-30. NEW: Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide (Columbia River to Stevens Pass, 2000, p.276), via Google Books search-inside snippets: 'Southeast Face was climbed by Curt Snyder and Kevin Kurtz on July 3, 1986; one pitch (5.6) climbs a chimney under loose blocks and on to the upper slabs.' The next entry is 'WEST BUTTRESS: By Charles Sink and Eric Gerber on July 4, 1971'. So Line B (Southeast Face, one pitch 5.6) is a named, separately credited route in the guidebook. The peak page's 'Southeast Face goes up the white rock one pitch 5.6' agrees on face, pitch count and grade. But that page's route list is drawn from Beckey, so it is not clearly independent. 'White rock' appears only on the peak page; Beckey says a chimney under loose blocks, then slabs. Line A (East Face, 4th class, zig-zag ledges, reverse to descend) still has only the route database. Snippet searches of Beckey for a Witches Tower East Face / 4th-class / ledges line found none; the only 'East Face' hits on that page belong to Boola Boola Buttress. The cascadeclimbers threads that now load in the browser give nothing citable. 2006 'Witches Tower?': one poster recalls a 4th-class way up from Beckey; another describes an easy scramble 'on (I believe) the southeast side', a ramp to small chimneys, no rope, walked off toward Little Annapurna - that is the scramble, not either line. 2003 'Witch's Tower': the main route 'goes up the se side ... ridge/ramp/arete' (hearsay); another party climbed ~4 pitches of ~5.5 on the SW. 2010 Enchantments tour: a class 3 walk-up. No search found the 2008 'Parade Route' report, and the forum's own search requires login (not used). Result: Line B now has its primary guidebook source plus a restatement that is probably derived from it; Line A still has one source. The condition for the strip ops (Line A gets a second source and Line B does not) is NOT met - if anything it is the reverse - so no ops. Beckey's text confirms the row joins two different routes: a 4th-class ledge system (A) and a credited 1986 one-pitch 5.6 chimney-and-slab line (B). Recommendation: split the row. Or, if the owner accepts the guidebook plus the peak page as two sources, re-point this row to Beckey's Southeast Face (5.6, one pitch). The 4th-class East Face rests on one source either way.
sources: Google Books search-inside: Beckey, Cascade Alpine Guide: Columbia River to Stevens Pass (2000) p.276
